paper_title: Revisiting the bound on axion-photon coupling from Globular Clusters
notes: Headline bound from Eq. (3) and abstract: g_agamma < 0.66e-10 GeV^-1 at 95% CL, from analysis of the R parameter in 39 Galactic Globular Clusters. Reported as a flat (mass-independent) limit, which is the standard form for Primakoff stellar-cooling bounds on ALPs. Valid for axion/ALP masses where Primakoff production in HB stellar cores is efficient (m_a below ~a few keV; upper edge set here at 1e4 eV as the approximate stellar core temperature scale). The paper notes the GC bound is the strongest constraint for generic ALPs except in the extremely low mass region m_a < ~1e-7 eV where SN1987A gamma-ray bounds are stronger, but the GC bound itself extends to arbitrarily low mass, so the flat line is drawn from 1e-10 eV. Astrophysical (stellar) bound, independent of dark-matter density. 68% CL value is g_agamma = 0.45(+0.12/-0.16)e-10 GeV^-1 (Eq. 2); reported the 95% CL headline value.
